section_summary.extract_value: This abstract reports validation of the German Body Appreciation Scale (BAS) in a community sample of 156 women and 144 men in Austria, showing good internal reliability and a unidimensional factor structure. It notes that women (but not men) showed an inverse association between BMI and body appreciation and reports a small sex difference favoring men (Cohen's d = 0.26). The abstract does not report survey method, mean age, ethnicity percentages, or numeric correlations between BAS and BMI.
section_summary.evidence_source: This paper examined the psychometric properties of the German version of the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS), a novel scale for the assessment of positive body image. Based on a community sample of 156 women and 144 men in Austria, results showed good internal reliability and construct validity for the BAS scores, as well as a unidimensional factor structure for both women and men. In addition, women with lower BMIs reported greater body appreciation, but no such association was found for men. Finally, there were small sex differences in BAS scores, with men scoring more positively than women (Cohen's d = 0.26).
